summary.text: David Eastman is a Republican candidate for the Alaska House of Representatives, District 27, in the November 3, 2026 general election, and a former member of the House who served from 2017 to 2025.
A West Point graduate and former U.S. Army officer, he lives in Wasilla.

paragraphs.text: David Eastman was born in Orange County, California, and lives in Wasilla, Alaska.

He earned a bachelor's degree from West Point in 2003, a graduate degree from Biola University in 2008 and a graduate degree from the Acton School of Business in 2019, and he served in the U.S. Army from 2002 to 2009.
In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, he said he chose Alaska as his first assignment as an Army officer and that he lives in Wasilla with his wife Jennifer and their four children.

Eastman first won election to the Alaska House of Representatives in 2016, defeating Democrat Patricia Faye-Brazel in District 10, and he won re-election there in 2020 over Democrat Monica Stein-Olson.
In 2022 he won a seat representing District 27 with 51.3 percent of the vote in a ranked-choice general election.
In the 2023-2024 legislative session he was assigned to the House Judiciary Committee.
He lost the 2024 general election in District 27 to Jubilee Underwood, 48.1 percent to 50.6 percent, and left office on January 21, 2025.

In the August 18, 2026 nonpartisan primary, Eastman received 45.4 percent of the vote and advanced to the general election alongside incumbent Jubilee Underwood, a fellow Republican, who received 54.6 percent.
In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey, he listed his priorities as the Permanent Fund Dividend, public safety and justice, and integrity in government institutions.
